# AST test-only candidate audit

Snapshot: codex/world-aware-tools at 6f584a8f0 plus the shorthand-reference correction for #2511. Package source matched main at 8fc4667aa when checked; some test/tooling files differ.

Command: `pnpm ast testonly '' --json --max 10000`. Exit 0, status complete, 3,435 package files scanned; 147/147 candidate exports displayed. Separate declared-test-seam bucket: 39. Runtime: 79.20 seconds.

Before correction: 150 candidates. After: 147. Only collapseNewlines, trimTrailingWhitespace, and dropIncompleteSentence were removed; they have live same-file shorthand dispatch-table references. No additions.

## What these results establish

The lens finds exports with test consumption and no recognized production consumption or own-file reference. It is not application-entry transitive reachability. A production import in an unreachable module can still keep an export alive; namespace/dynamic imports can conservatively keep surfaces alive. UI availability, framework-loaded config, type-only declarations, and deliberate test adapters require separate judgment. This is a candidate inventory, not a deletion manifest.

## Checked application examples

- Recent-models store: pushRecentModel/useRecentModels have no detected production consumer; the state barrel re-exports them and tests exercise the MRU behavior. This is an unwired app capability worth deciding whether to use or retire.
- useDeleteRefinerySession: invoked from the refinery CT story; production barrel re-exports it. Its comment explicitly records future surface intent.
- ensureUserSettings: tests call the eager seed primitive. Its comment explicitly says no current app callers; the production write path has its own guarded seed.
- subscribeTurnSlot and loadPendingTurns: comments explicitly explain test observation/query roles. They are not proof that streaming or pending-turn processing is dead.

Corroboration used AST liveness, ast-grep TS/TSX identifier scans and literal searches over packages/tests/scripts/tooling (7,829 TS/TSX files listed by rg). This spot-check does not adjudicate every inventory row.
